## MCP Configuration — IDE-Agnostic Setup

The **canonical standard** for project-level MCP is `.mcp.json` in the repo root, using the `{"mcpServers": {...}}` schema. This is recognized across IDEs and tools.

### File layout after changes

| File | Format | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| [`.mcp.json`](file://~/projects/playground/hackathon/google/hackathon-builder-cup-manufacturing-anomaly/.mcp.json) | `{"mcpServers": {...}}` | **Canonical** — Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, Antigravity, and most MCP tools |
| [`.agents/mcp_config.json`](file://~/projects/playground/hackathon/google/hackathon-builder-cup-manufacturing-anomaly/.agents/mcp_config.json) | `{"mcpServers": {...}}` | **Antigravity** workspace-level config (same schema, picked up from `.agents/`) |
| [`.vscode/mcp.json`](file://~/projects/playground/hackathon/google/hackathon-builder-cup-manufacturing-anomaly/.vscode/mcp.json) | `{"servers": {...}}` | **VS Code only** — kept working, with a comment pointing to the canonical file |

### Why two files for the same server?

- `.mcp.json` (root) = **project-level standard** that travels with the repo and works across IDEs
- `.agents/mcp_config.json` = **Antigravity-specific** pickup path; uses identical content so there's no drift

> [!TIP]
> Going forward, add new MCP servers to `.mcp.json` first, then mirror into `.agents/mcp_config.json` and `.vscode/mcp.json`. All three use the same server config block — only the outer key differs (`mcpServers` vs `servers` for VS Code).

I can see the problem — there's a hardcoded API key in the global config. **Yes, environment variables work**, and that's the right approach. Here's the full picture:

---

## Best Practices: No Inline API Keys in MCP Config

### How it works — `env` block + shell env vars

The MCP `env` block injects environment variables **into the server process**. For SSE/remote servers with headers, you reference shell env vars using `$VAR_NAME` syntax (supported by Antigravity and most MCP hosts).

**Pattern 1 — `env` block (for stdio servers)**
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-server": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "my-mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "API_KEY": "${MY_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
The server process gets `API_KEY` from your shell environment.

**Pattern 2 — Header value via env var (for SSE/remote servers)**
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "stitch": {
      "serverUrl": "https://stitch.googleapis.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Goog-Api-Key": "${STITCH_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> [!WARNING]
> The `${VAR}` interpolation in `headers` depends on whether your MCP host supports it. Antigravity does. Claude Desktop does **not** — it only interpolates in `env` blocks for stdio servers.

---

### Recommended setup

**Step 1 — Store the key in your shell profile / secret manager**

```zsh
# ~/.zshrc (or use 1Password, macOS Keychain, direnv, etc.)
export STITCH_API_KEY="AQ.Ab8RN6JSUSYZIseZ195TooXz6T_WglXXY48926lfgd-rMuG8tg"
```

**Step 2 — Reference it in the config**

Update your global config:

Done. Now set the variable in your shell:

The variable isn't in your shell profile yet. You need to add it:

```zsh
# Add to ~/.zshrc
echo 'export STITCH_API_KEY="AQ.Ab8RN6JSUSYZIseZ195TooXz6T_WglXXY48926lfgd-rMuG8tg"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
```

> [!CAUTION]
> The original key (`AQ.Ab8...`) was committed/saved in plaintext. **Rotate it** if it was ever pushed to git or shared — treat it as compromised.

---

### Tiered best practices (pick your level)

| Approach | Security | Convenience | Works with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `~/.zshrc` export | ✅ Not in repo | ✅ Simple | All IDEs |
| [`direnv`](https://direnv.net/) + `.envrc` | ✅ Per-project | ✅ Auto-loaded | All IDEs |
| macOS Keychain + `security` CLI | ✅✅ OS-secured | ⚠️ Script needed | All IDEs |
| 1Password CLI (`op run`) | ✅✅✅ Vault | ⚠️ Op CLI needed | stdio servers |

**`direnv` is the sweet spot for project-level secrets** — you put secrets in `.envrc` (git-ignored), and they're auto-exported whenever you `cd` into the project.

```bash
# .envrc (git-ignored!)
export STITCH_API_KEY="..."
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="./service-account.json"
```

```bash
# .gitignore — make sure this is there
.envrc
```
